children: Australian stocks look set to rise at the open, lifting from a three-month low despite a soft lead from U.S. equities. Local futures are up by almost 0.4% ahead of Wednesday's session, suggesting that the S&P/ASX 200 will recover some of its 0.9% deficit of the prior session. The benchmark index is down by 4.5% so far in September amid growing expectations that the country's central bank will resume interest-rate rises at its next board meeting. Ahead of the open, building-materials supplier James Hardie said it expected to generate US$125 million of synergies a year earlier than previously anticipated. U.S. stocks fell ahead of the Fed's rate decision later this week. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
